eslint-plugin-svelte's processor needs this rule for `settings.svelte.ignoreWarnings`: what the rules named there report in the markup of a component is removed from the results. What they report in the scripts stays. Each entry is a rule ID, or a regular expression in a string, such as `"/^svelte\\//"`.

The rule reports a setting that isn't an array of strings, at the start of the component.

It needs the processor of `eslint-plugin-svelte`, `processor: "svelte/svelte"`: without it the rule does nothing.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. It runs on the Svelte components that an ESLint config lints with `svelte-eslint-parser`, in the place of the rule of `eslint-plugin-svelte`:

{/* skip */}

```js eslint.config.js
import svelte from "eslint-plugin-svelte";

export default [
  ...svelte.configs.recommended,
  { rules: { "svelte/system": "error" } },
];
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported, with `settings.svelte.ignoreWarnings` set to `"no-undef"`:

{/* bad {"processor": true, "settings": {"svelte": {"ignoreWarnings": "no-undef"}}} */}

```svelte
<p>{user.name}</p>
```

Not reported, with `["no-undef"]`:

{/* good {"processor": true, "settings": {"svelte": {"ignoreWarnings": ["no-undef"]}}} */}

```svelte
<p>{user.name}</p>
```

With `settings.svelte.ignoreWarnings` set to `["no-undef"]` and `no-undef` on, `user` is reported in the script and not in the markup:

{/* skip */}

```svelte
<script>
  console.log(user);
</script>

<p>{user.name}</p>
```
